clue.text: La Traviata's bloomer

parts.note: Verdi's opera comes from the Dumas story La Dame aux Camélias, so the flower that heroine wears is the one meant

explanation.surface: A question about a blunder made in Verdi's opera La Traviata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but it is a flower: Verdi's heroine Violetta is the 'lady of the camellias' of the Dumas source.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowering shrub carried by the courtesan in the Dumas story behind Verdi's opera is this bloom.

clue.text: A swan-song for him?

parts.note: a swan-song is a final performance, a last air or tune

explanation.surface: A final performance dedicated to a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair is a man's first name, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: As in thè TUC, is unusually zealous

indicators.note: unusually tells us the letters of the five preceding words appear in an unusual order

parts.note: the newspaper prints 'the' with a stray accent

explanation.surface: Trade unionists at the TUC, the Trades Union Congress, are oddly keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Being zealous means full of eager devotion, just as being keen and eager is.

clue.text: Author needs material about architect

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the fabric word wraps around the architect

parts.note: lace is a fine open fabric
Sir Christopher Wren was the architect of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A writer requires fabric relating to a building designer.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence was a novelist (and T. E. Lawrence wrote too), so the surname fits a writer.

clue.text: Try to read a dry letter on training

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the training piece below, after the letter

parts.note: TT (teetotal) means not drinking, dry
em is the name of the letter M
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: An effort to read a text while sober and exercising.
explanation.definitionFit: To try is to make an effort at something, the same as having a go.

clue.text: Cable from a shrew, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words before it can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Wiring made from a small mammal, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Trunk of sound wood

indicators.note: sound means heard, so we want a word pronounced like the one for a wooden ball

parts.note: a wood is a bowl in the game of bowls

explanation.surface: Part of a healthy tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound wood' reads as healthy timber, but 'sound' is the homophone signal and a 'wood' is a ball in bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: The bole is the main stem of a tree below its branches.

clue.text: Veteran hunter got wound?

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover, so an aged one being wound up is an elderly timepiece

explanation.surface: An experienced huntsman was injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' suggests injury, but it is the past tense of wind: a hunter is a pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience, and an aged watch is an old clock-like device too.

clue.text: Fall in work-product of whaling

indicators.note: in tells us the word for falling weather sits inside the word for labour

parts.note: toil means hard work
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A slip at work, followed by a note about what the whaling industry produced.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil rendered from whale blubber was the chief commodity the whaling trade sold.

clue.text: Awkward situation for one bound for the guillotine

explanation.surface: A guess at the predicament of someone condemned in the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the cart' is British slang for being in trouble; tumbrils, open carts, took the condemned to the guillotine.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang 'in the cart' means in trouble; and a tumbril, a farm wagon, carried victims to the guillotine.

clue.text: Londoner's way to get rid of ill-feeling

definitions.text: Londoner's way to get rid of ill-feeling

parts.words: Londoner's way to get rid of ill-feeling
parts.note: read 'way' as a road and 'ill-feeling' as sickness: the London road famous for private doctors

explanation.surface: Advice on how a Londoner might shake off resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' looks like resentment, but it means being unwell; the London street lined with private medical practices is where you go to be cured.
explanation.definitionFit: This central London road is synonymous with private medical consultants, where people go for treatment.

clue.text: Free gin distribution settles needs of yachtsman, perhaps

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: distribution means sharing out, so the three letters of gin are scattered into a new order

parts.note: lights means settles or alights, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Handing out complimentary gin keeps a sailor's wants in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps shown by a vessel at anchor are required at sea, so a sailor needs them.

clue.text: Members of family in a jam?

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal
a son is a male child in a family

explanation.surface: Relatives who find themselves in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a jam' seems to mean in trouble, but it means inside a preserve: this plum is made into jam.
explanation.definitionFit: This small dark plum is a classic fruit for preserves, so it is what you find in that sort of jam.

clue.text: Eccentric Agadir MP, for example

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of line, telling us to rearrange the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A peculiar Member of Parliament from the Moroccan city of Agadir held up as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a model or pattern, a standard instance of something.

clue.text: Made and packed without direction

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the packing word goes around the compass point

parts.note: crated means packed into crates
E (east) is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Goods were produced and boxed up with no instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something is to bring it into being, the same as having brought it forth.

clue.text: Someone to engage to produce pamphlet

parts.note: a chap is a person, someone
to book is to engage, as a performer

explanation.surface: Hiring a person to write a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapbooks were small cheap pamphlets of tales or ballads sold by pedlars.

clue.text: Revolver in pitched battle?

parts.note: read as cricket: a bowler who makes the ball turn after it bounces on the pitch

explanation.surface: A handgun being fired during a fierce fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a pistol and 'pitched battle' a fight, but it is a cricket match, where a slow bowler makes the ball rotate off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a slow bowler imparts rotation to the ball so it turns off the pitch, hence this name.

clue.text: Mitigate a bad upset in the head

indicators.note: in puts the article and turned word for bad inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: ill means bad

explanation.surface: Ease a nasty disturbance in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease or lessen pain or severity, as to mitigate does.

clue.text: Perhaps he worked on paper edited by 25

explanation.surface: A writer who once worked for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Leigh Hunt (25) edited The Examiner, a radical weekly; an exam marker works on candidates' papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker of exam scripts goes through papers; and The Examiner was the weekly that Leigh Hunt ran.

clue.text: Opposed to using gas in TA manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving around, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Objecting to chemical weapons in Territorial Army exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means you oppose it.

clue.text: Helping wrongdoer in a transaction of course

parts.note: betting is the trade done at a racecourse

explanation.surface: Assisting a criminal during a deal, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally', but it means 'at a racecourse'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage someone in committing a crime.

clue.text: Resident is batting to end of game

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
mate (checkmate) ends a chess game

explanation.surface: A local is at the crease until the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the cricket term for the side currently batting.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone living in an institution such as a prison or asylum.

clue.text: She gets one pound twice a quarter

indicators.note: twice says the pair made from pound and one appears two times over

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (from libra)
I is the Roman numeral for one
N (north) is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A woman receives a pound twice every three months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' suggests three months, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilian is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Preparing prince for battle at Crécy, or criminal activity?

definitions.text: Preparing prince for battle at Crécy

explanation.surface: Either the Black Prince arming for a famous medieval battle or something illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Prince, Edward III's son, fought at Crécy in 1346; putting him into chain mail splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion by threatening to reveal secrets is a crime; and dressing the Black Prince in armour for Crécy fits the split reading.

clue.text: Take off number from top

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or take off
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Remove a figure from the highest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like 'remove', but it means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Essayist enjoyed by Jorrocks

explanation.surface: A writer who was a favourite of a famous comic character.
explanation.walkthrough: Leigh Hunt was a Romantic-era essayist; John Jorrocks is the fox-hunting grocer in R. S. Surtees's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Leigh Hunt wrote essays; and the Surtees grocer Jorrocks loved riding to hounds after foxes.

clue.text: Perhaps gives fresh heart to see ARP reorganized

indicators.note: reorganized means rearranged, so the letters of the three preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An encouraging word about restructuring Air Raid Precautions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives fresh heart' looks like encouragement, but it means a surgeon doing a heart transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs surgery, and a heart transplant is one example of such work.

clue.text: Government department is about to back USA in test

indicators.note: in places the 'about' piece and the turned country inside the word for a test

parts.note: to try is to test
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: to back means to run backwards, so the letters of USA are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A ministry is about to support America in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: This UK ministry manages public finances and the economy, a major branch of government.
